newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat price continues fall in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: German wheat price continues fall in slow trade.

text.p: A lack of wheat export business and a lull in domestic sales continue to weigh on German wheat prices, brokers said on Wednesday.
With Brussels not yet ready to resume export subsidies and mounting pre-harvest pressure, they did not expect higher levels of activity over the next few weeks.
"We're emptying old crop stores, where our premium wheat is still in demand in southern Europe," one broker said.
"Fresh price impetus has to come from the world market because European crops can no longer fail badly, which means consumers are factoring in lower prices."
The Hamburg grain exchange cut its spot bread wheat price (12.5 percent protein, 220 hagberg) by five marks per tonne on the week to 267.50 marks, down 10 on the fortnight.
The feed wheat price also shed five marks to 265, compared with 275 two weeks earlier.
Feed wheat markets came under renewed pressure from British offers.
New crop markets eased in line with spot and because buyers were not forthcoming.
Fob Baltic sellers put nominal June delivery wheat at 270-282.50 marks (12 percent) and material with 13/14 percent protein at 277.50-322.50 marks.
Material with 12 percent has fallen from 285 to 270 marks this month but top qualities have held up at 322.50.
Fob Baltic barley and offers were little changed at 270 marks and 265-267.50 marks respectively.
New crop September wheat was now in a 270-305 marks range, depending on quality.
New crop rye (July/August) indications remained at around 260-265 marks and barley was set at 240 marks fob.
